h1: Agent Grove — AI & SaaS Landing Page Design
tagline: Landing page reference for an AI or SaaS product, captured at 1484x1080 with the layout, timings and palette specified in the brief.
summary: Landing page reference for an AI or SaaS product — a dark stage, React and Tailwind CSS, a stats row and 300ms transitions.
about: Agent Grove is the landing page reference for an AI or SaaS product, and the brief behind it is a full build spec rather than a mood board. The palette is black #2B2B2B underneath, set in Geist. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 1484x1080 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. The motion budget is 300ms transitions, cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) and a looping video bed. Treat it as the brief for an AI or SaaS product landing page that has to hold up under a rebuild, not just a first look.

layout.title: Top row: wordmark, links, one action
layout.body: The bar overlays the landing page instead of pushing it down, so the composition keeps the full height of the first screen. The bar sits over the 1484x1080 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: Every measurement is written down
layout.body: The brief states its sizes at capture (24px spacing steps, 300ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) easing), so a rebuild can be verified instead of approximated. The brief states values rather than proportions, so the composition keeps its relationships when the copy changes length.

layout.title: Cards do the structuring
layout.body: The grid does the reading order for you: panels of equal weight, one idea each, set in Geist at a small size so the structure stays visible. Headings inside the panels sit one step above their own body copy, not one step below the page headline.

layout.title: The footer is a full composition
layout.body: Links are grouped into columns with the wordmark in its own block, which keeps a long footer readable instead of turning it into a list. Type sizes step down from the column headings to the links, so the hierarchy survives a dense footer.

motion.title: Short, matched timings
motion.body: The controls resolve in 300ms, fast enough that the page answers as it is touched rather than after it. The quoted timing covers state changes, so the feedback is the part of the motion that is specified. One duration per behaviour.

motion.title: The loop does the ambient work
motion.body: Ambient movement comes from the 5.4s 1484x1080 loop rather than from scroll effects, which keeps the page calm and the type readable. A poster frame stands in when autoplay is blocked, so the motion is additive rather than required.

style.glass: Panels are translucent over black #2B2B2B, and the type on top stays at full contrast so the effect never costs readability.

editorial.title: Making the landing page yours
editorial.body: The composition is the reusable part and the subject is yours. Keep 24px spacing steps and 300ms transitions and replace the words, the media and the brand marks. The composition is the reusable part, and it survives a different brand.

editorial.title: How the landing page reflows
editorial.body: A fixed desktop scale would have been easier. The brief adds a clamp between 16px and 24px, which is what keeps the display line proportionate between widths. The reflow keeps the action reachable at every width.

editorial.title: The timing behind the landing page
editorial.body: A short motion budget costs you drama on the first frame. It buys legibility, and it means 300ms transitions, a 5.4s media loop and hover and press states can be ported without a library. Nothing animates for its own sake in this landing page.

faq.question: How long is the prompt behind Agent Grove?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 1484x1080, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

faq.question: Do I need React and Tailwind CSS to rebuild Agent Grove?
faq.answer: Agent Grove was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: Can I ship a page rebuilt from Agent Grove without crediting it?
faq.answer: The brief is a description, not a licence to redistribute someone else's assets. Keep the structure and the numbers, replace the media and the brand marks, and credit the source if a client asks where the layout came from. The reference was captured at 1484x1080.
